headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to remove U.S. troops from hostilities with Iran unless Congress approved them.
what_it_does: This resolution would have directed the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran. The troops could have stayed involved only if Congress passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force against Iran. It would not have stopped the United States from defending itself, its personnel, or its facilities in other countries against an attack. On March 18, 2026, the Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it, so it did not pass.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the U.S. Armed Forces
who_it_affects.how: Service members taking part in hostilities with Iran would have been withdrawn unless Congress authorized the action.
The President would have needed approval from Congress to continue military hostilities against Iran, except to defend against attacks.
Congress would have had to vote on a declaration of war or use-of-force authorization for hostilities against Iran to continue.
